title: Akbari
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rabbi Chananyah bar Akbari appears at the end of Jerusalem Talmud Terumot. Hyman argues that this is undoubtedly a town-name, as in Bava Metzia 24b and Avodah Zarah 30a: an Israelite would not be named after an unclean creeping creature. Although we use unclean animals’ names, this is because they appear in the Torah—for example, “Binyamin is a ravening wolf,” “Yehudah is a lion’s cub,” or “I shall be to them like a bear.” But people were not named after unclean creeping creatures, even though the mouse is mentioned in the Torah. As for Chuldah the prophetess, Megillah 14b indeed says on this point: “There were two arrogant women, and their names were hateful.”

notes.text: The claim about animal-derived names and the certainty that Akbari is a town-name are Hyman’s reasoning. ע״ז here means “on this point,” not the tractate Avodah Zarah.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 11 names Rabbi Chananyah bar Akbari with Rabbi Chiyya of Tzippori in the burning-oil account. This does not establish Hyman’s universal naming rule or his “undoubtedly” town-name conclusion; both remain his reasoning. The Biblical Achbor comparison is not an identity admission.
